prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: original material-led illustration for gold-wire colour-paste decorative art in Dezhou, Shandong.
Primary request: ONE complete original decorative panel with thin gold-coloured wire-like boundaries enclosing gently textured coloured fill, arranged as an invented abstract flower-and-leaf design. This is an AI imagination about the materials, not an actual workshop artwork or evidence of a precise technique.
Subject and composition: one landscape panel rests almost face-on against a quiet warm-paper ground. Its full outer edge is visible with roomy margins. Within it, a restrained asymmetrical spray of broad flowers and leaves curves through open negative space. Very thin raised golden contour lines enclose matte granular colour-filled shapes; visible small-scale paste or pigment texture, subtle shadows where the wire meets the fill, quiet ivory, mineral blue-green, dusky coral and a few restrained gold highlights. Keep the coloured areas tactile and matte, not jewel-encrusted metal. The panel is flat decorative art, not a vase, rug, fabric sample, woven tapestry, jewellery or metal casting.
Style: contemporary editorial material illustration, shallow relief, natural soft light, beautiful readable thin boundaries, clearly different from woven gold thread. Do not turn it into a cloisonne-enamel manufacturing explanation or show tools, glue bottles, hands or work steps. Invent all motifs and no known artist's style or existing work is copied.
Authenticity: do not attribute to Li Aimin or a local studio; no ownership, age, heritage-level or technique claims in the image. The physical appearance is creative, not a verified recipe or production method.
Single standalone creative artwork, not a page, diagram, contact sheet or UI. Horizontal 3:2, ideally native 1536x1024. Keep complete subject silhouettes and generous safe margins; fully readable when shown with contain on mobile. No people, real faces, hands, text, pseudo-writing, labels, numbers, seals, signatures, brands, logos or watermark. No copied artwork, named craftsperson's work, museum object or process documentation.
